title: Tech Connectivity
intro: Two countries, two connectivity profiles. China blocks Google, WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, Gmail, and Google Maps. Install and test VPN BEFORE entering China — app stores are blocked in-country. Vietnam has no restrictions. eSIM is the cleanest multi-country solution for US travelers.

tables.caption: Connectivity Options
rows: Airalo or Holafly — China ~$15–25 (5–10 GB, 15 days); Vietnam ~$10–18 (5–10 GB); buy QR codes before travel; activate on landing
China Unicom at PEK (~¥100/10 GB); Viettel/Vietnamobile at Noi Bai (~$5/5 GB); requires SIM swap at border
Airalo eSIM — manage from phone before departure; no SIM swapping; keep US physical SIM for iMessage/SMS

tables.caption: China VPN — CRITICAL
rows: Most reliable; obfuscation protocol gets through Great Firewall
Specifically tuned for China; slightly more expensive

tables.caption: Power & Plugs
rows: US devices mostly work (check 100–240V on charger); universal adapter
One universal adapter (Anker/Belkin); 20,000 mAh USB-C power bank for Great Wall and Hội An walking days

tables.caption: Digital Security
rows: Use VPN on ALL China WiFi; hotel WiFi safer but still use VPN
Avoid for banking; use eSIM data instead
Scan passports, visas, insurance → iCloud/Google Drive before China entry; email to self
Instagram, WhatsApp, Twitter only via VPN
Notify all banks/credit cards of travel to China AND Vietnam before departure

tables.caption: Payment Apps
rows: WeChat Pay (link US Visa/MC before arrival), Alipay, Cash (¥), Visa/MC at 4–5 star hotels
AmEx less accepted; many vendors WeChat/Alipay only
Credit cards at 4–5 star hotels/restaurants; Grab app payment; Cash (₫) for street food

bullets.heading: Offline Kit — China
items: Baidu Maps — offline navigation (English interface); replaces Google Maps
DiDi — Chinese Uber; link US credit card before arrival
WeChat — payments + vendor/hotel communication
Google Translate — Chinese (Simplified) offline pack; camera mode for menus
Hotel addresses in Chinese script saved as offline phone notes

bullets.heading: Offline Kit — Vietnam
items: Grab — book in advance; better and cheaper than taxis
Maps.me — offline maps for rural areas
Google Maps — works normally; download offline for Hanoi, Đà Nẵng, Hội An
Google Translate — Vietnamese offline pack
Hotel address cards in Vietnamese for Grab/taxis

bullets.heading: VPN Setup Checklist
items: Download VPN app on both phones at home (iOS/Android)
Purchase subscription; test connection through Chinese servers
Save VPN credentials in offline password manager (not Google)
Set VPN to auto-connect on WiFi
Expect 20–40% speed reduction — acceptable for Google Maps, WhatsApp, Gmail

bullets.heading: Pre-Departure Checklist
items: Install/test VPN; purchase Airalo eSIMs for China and Vietnam
Install DiDi, Grab, WeChat (link US credit card)
Download offline translation packs; Baidu Maps; Maps.me Vietnam
Notify banks; scan passports/visas/insurance to cloud
Confirm dual-voltage chargers; pack universal adapter + power bank

callouts.text: Must install VPN BEFORE entering China — app stores blocked in-country
Multi-currency cards: Charles Schwab debit (zero ATM fees) or Wise card — carry both
Connectivity, VPN, offline apps, plugs, payments, and security covered for both countries
